title: Pillars of Salah: ruku‘, sajdah and the last sitting
intro: The last three parts of Salah.

learn.html: We bend to half the body so our back is straight. We hold our knees – boys with fingers spread, girls with fingers together. We look at our toes and say three times:

learn.label: In ruku‘ (3×)
learn.en: Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great!

learn.html: We first put the knees down, then the palms, and last the forehead and nose. The hands are a face-width apart. In sajdah the toes are bent and stay on the ground, heels together. Boys keep their elbows off the ground; girls keep them almost on the ground. We say three times:

learn.label: In sajdah (3×)
learn.en: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High!

learn.html: Prayers of two rak‘ahs have one sitting; prayers of three or four rak‘ahs have two. In the sitting we look at our hands on our knees. Boys sit on the left foot with the right foot upright, toes toward the Qiblah. Girls turn both feet to the right side. In the last sitting of every prayer we recite At-Tahiyyat, the salawat and the duas.

learn.title: ⭐ The finger
learn.html: In At-Tahiyyat, at laa ilaaha we fold the fingers of the right hand and point the index finger; at illallaah we lower it.

questions.q: How many times do we say the tasbih in ruku‘?
How many sittings does a 4-rak‘ah prayer have?
What do we recite in the last sitting?
options: At-Tahiyyat, the salawat and the duas

questions.q: When do we raise the index finger?

practice.title: Questions to talk about
prompts: 💬 What are the pillars of Salah? When is Salah not right?
🧍 Show ruku‘, sajdah and the sitting the right way.
💬 What makes one rak‘ah? How many rak‘ahs can a Salah have?
